title: The Agent Development Life Cycle — Zack Reneau-Wedeen, Sierra
talk_summary: Zack Reneau-Wedeen describes Sierra's 'Agent Development Life Cycle', a software-development-lifecycle analog for LLM agents where production conversations are reviewed, defects become filed issues, issues become regression tests, and releases only ship once tests pass. He stresses that AI is now applied to each stage of that loop (dev, testing, QA) and that agents are treated as products with dedicated engineering/PM functions.

takeaways.what_they_do: Every reviewed production conversation that reveals a defect is filed as an issue, which automatically spawns a test; the fix ships only once that test passes, so the test suite grows from a handful to thousands over time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can report this issue it then will lead to an issue being filed which leads to a test being created and then once that test is passing we can make a new release
takeaways.numbers: agents go from 'a handful of tests at launch to hundreds and then thousands of tests'

takeaways.what_they_do: A dedicated 'experience manager' lets operators dive into every conversation, see high-level reports of agent behavior in real time, and attach feedback directly to the transcript that becomes an issue.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can dive in and look at every conversation and you can look at high level reports of how is the agent forming in real time

takeaways.technique: Apply AI to every ADLC stage, not just coding
takeaways.what_they_do: They explicitly add AI assistance to development, testing, and QA stages of the loop rather than only code generation, using reasoning models as a 'force multiplier' at each step.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're actually able to add AI to each part of this life cycle and speed up the improvements

takeaways.technique: Treat agent as product with dedicated eng/PM functions
takeaways.what_they_do: Sierra assigns dedicated agent-engineering and agent-product-management roles forward-deployed with customers, iterating daily rather than treating the agent as a drag-and-drop config.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have dedicated agent engineering and agent product management functions that you can think of sort of as forward deployed

takeaways.what_they_do: They frame LLMs as 'building on a foundation of jello' — non-deterministic, slow, expensive — and deliberately invoke traditional deterministic software where helpful rather than expecting the model to be reliable.
takeaways.evidence_quote: large language models are like building on top of a foundation of jello
